tasks.title: REGEXP_INSTR/REGEXP_SUBSTR/REGEXP_REPLACE truncate pos and occurrence to 32-bit int: occurrence 4294967298 acts as 2

classification.basis: Exact saved kind mapping; not execution readiness

source_review_decision.reason: 三条REGEXP边界查询完整，可直接观察大occurrence/pos被截成32位的异常。

test_spec.setup: 独立会话，使用cmain给定短ASCII字符串和正则，固定字符集/排序规则。
test_spec.steps: 执行REGEXP_INSTR occurrence=4与4294967298、pos=4294967297及REGEXP_REPLACE occurrence=4294967297；保存输出和错误码。
test_spec.oracle: 超出匹配次数应无匹配，越界pos应按接口语义报错，不能静默等同低32位位置并命中或替换已有匹配。
requirements: 不由客户端窄化大整数字面量
test_spec.target_applicability: 目标版本具备ICU正则函数，是否同样截断待执行。

explicit_requirements: 不由客户端窄化大整数字面量

source.title: REGEXP_INSTR/REGEXP_SUBSTR/REGEXP_REPLACE truncate pos and occurrence to 32-bit int: occurrence 4294967298 acts as 2

header.Bug #121522: REGEXP_INSTR/REGEXP_SUBSTR/REGEXP_REPLACE truncate pos and occurrence to 32-bit int: occurrence 4294967298 acts as 2

comments.author: Ke Han
comments.text:
Description:
The pos and occurrence arguments of REGEXP_INSTR(), REGEXP_SUBSTR() and
REGEXP_REPLACE() are read into an int, so only their low 32 bits are used:

occurrence -- 'abcabcabc' has three matches of 'a+':

  SELECT REGEXP_INSTR('abcabcabc','a+',1,2);            -- 4
  SELECT REGEXP_INSTR('abcabcabc','a+',1,4);            -- 0   (no 4th match: correct)
  SELECT REGEXP_INSTR('abcabcabc','a+',1,4294967298);   -- 4   (2^32+2 acts as 2)
  SELECT REGEXP_INSTR('abcabcabc','a+',1,4294967296);   -- 1   (2^32 acts as 0 -> 1)
  SELECT REGEXP_INSTR('abcabcabc','a+',1,2147483648);   -- 1   (2^31 is negative -> 1)
  SELECT REGEXP_INSTR('abcabcabc','a+',1,9223372036854775809);   -- 1
  SELECT REGEXP_SUBSTR('ab ac ad','A.',1,4);            -- NULL (correct)
  SELECT REGEXP_SUBSTR('ab ac ad','A.',1,4294967298);   -- 'ac'
  SELECT REGEXP_REPLACE('aaabbccbbddaa','b+','x',1,3);            -- 'aaabbccbbddaa' (correct)
  SELECT REGEXP_REPLACE('aaabbccbbddaa','b+','x',1,4294967297);   -- 'aaaxccbbddaa'

pos -- a position past the end of the string is an error, but 2^32 + k is
position k:

  SELECT REGEXP_INSTR('abcabcabc','b+',10);             -- ERROR 3686 Index out of bounds
  SELECT REGEXP_INSTR('abcabcabc','b+',2147483648);     -- ERROR 3686
  SELECT REGEXP_INSTR('abcabcabc','b+',4294967297);     -- 2   (acts as pos 1)
  SELECT REGEXP_INSTR('abcabcabc','b+',4294967300);     -- 5   (acts as pos 4)
  SELECT REGEXP_SUBSTR('ab ac ad','A.',4294967299);     -- 'ac'
  SELECT REGEXP_REPLACE('aaabbccbbddaa','b+','x',4294967297,0);   -- 'aaaxccxddaa'

The same happens when the argument comes from a BIGINT column:

  CREATE TABLE t27 (id INT PRIMARY KEY, o BIGINT UNSIGNED);
  INSERT INTO t27 VALUES (1, 4), (2, 4294967298);
  SELECT id, REGEXP_INSTR('abcabcabc','a+',1,o), REGEXP_SUBSTR('abcabcabc','a+',1,o)
  FROM t27 ORDER BY id;
  -- 1  0  NULL
  -- 2  4  'a'

No warning in any case.  The other string functions that take positions and
counts (LEFT, RIGHT, SUBSTRING, LPAD, REPEAT, SPACE, ...) had the same 32-bit
narrowing and were fixed long ago (Bug #10963); REGEXP_* came later.

Where (trunk 3b99be40): sql/item_regexp_func.h

  115    std::optional<int> position() const {
  118        const int value = args[the_index]->val_int();
  ...
  134    std::optional<int> occurrence() const {
  137        const int value = args[the_index]->val_int();

How to repeat:
SELECT REGEXP_INSTR('abcabcabc','a+',1,4), REGEXP_INSTR('abcabcabc','a+',1,4294967298);
SELECT REGEXP_INSTR('abcabcabc','b+',4294967297);
SELECT REGEXP_REPLACE('aaabbccbbddaa','b+','x',1,4294967297);

-- expected: 0, 0 / ERROR 3686 / 'aaabbccbbddaa'
-- actual:   0, 4 / 2          / 'aaaxccbbddaa'

Suggested fix:
Read pos and occurrence as longlong (taking unsigned_flag into account).  A pos
larger than the subject length + 1 raises ER_REGEXP_INDEX_OUTOFBOUNDS_ERROR as it
does today for 10; an occurrence larger than INT_MAX can be clamped to INT_MAX
(there can never be that many matches), which gives "no match".
